scenes.headline: How Instella-MoE gates attention and hides communication
scenes.sub: A mixture of experts trained from pretraining to RL on AMD GPUs.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Doodle! Instella-MoE is a sixteen-billion-parameter mixture of experts, trained start to finish on AMD GPUs. Two ideas make it tick.

scenes.label: Two ideas
scenes.text: A learned gate trims attention's output for each token, and experts are routed on a slightly stale activation, so communication overlaps compute instead of waiting.
scenes.say: A learned gate trims attention's output for each token. And experts are routed on a slightly stale activation, so communication overlaps compute instead of waiting for it.

steps.say: Twenty-seven layers, each attention then a mixture of experts. Only two point eight billion parameters are active per token.
Every token runs two shared experts, and a router picks six more out of sixty-four.

scenes.title: Gated MLA: a per-token filter on attention

steps.say: Latent attention squeezes keys and values into a small latent, then looks up what the token needs.
Separately, one linear projection reads the same token and makes a gate, one value per channel.
The gate multiplies attention's output before the output projection. Attention decides what to look at; the gate decides how much to keep.

scenes.title: FarSkip-Collective: route on a stale copy

left.title: Fresh activation
items: Route on this layer's fresh output
All-to-all waits for compute to finish
GPUs idle while the network works
left.say: Normally a layer routes on its fresh attention output, so tokens can't cross GPUs until compute finishes. Compute and communication take turns.

right.title: Deliberately stale
items: Route on an outdated, partial activation
Trained end to end to expect it
right.say: FarSkip routes on a slightly stale copy that already exists, so the all-to-all runs alongside compute. The model is trained to expect it.

scenes.label: pretraining throughput from overlapping expert-parallel communication
scenes.note: and up to 39.2% lower time to first token when serving
scenes.say: AMD reports twelve point seven percent more pretraining throughput, and up to thirty-nine point two percent lower time to first token.

scenes.title: Base model average score, OLMES
scenes.note: AMD's own runs; training compute is not disclosed
scenes.say: As a base model, it lands second, behind Qwen3.5 and ahead of every fully open peer. What the run cost is still undisclosed.

scenes.text: FarSkip doesn't make the network faster. It makes the network's timing not matter, by feeding activations that are a step behind.
scenes.say: FarSkip doesn't make the network faster. It makes the network's timing not matter.

recap: A per-token gate on attention's output
Stale routing lets communication overlap compute
scenes.say: To recap: a sparse stack, a gate on attention, and routing on stale activations to hide the network.
